title: nicht and kein
definition: Nicht and kein both make statements negative, but they are used differently. Kein usually negates a noun with ein/eine or a noun with no article; nicht negates verbs, adjectives, adverbs, or a specific part of a sentence.

rules.title: Use kein with nouns
rules.explanation: Kein means 'no' or 'not a'. Its nominative forms are kein (masculine/neuter), keine (feminine/plural).

rules.title: Use nicht to negate an action or description
rules.explanation: Nicht is used with verbs, adjectives, adverbs, and many other sentence elements. Its position depends on what is being negated.

rules.title: nicht or kein?
rules.explanation: If the meaning is 'not a/no + noun', use kein. If you are saying an action or quality is not true, use nicht.

examples.note: Accusative example: keinen is used because Bruder is the direct object.

rules.title: Negating a specific item
rules.explanation: Nicht can appear before the part of the sentence being contrasted or emphasized.

examples.german: Ich fahre nicht heute, sondern morgen.
examples.english: I'm not going today, but tomorrow.

examples.note: Kaffee is negated as a noun; accusative masculine form keinen.

common_mistakes.explanation: Use kein to negate a noun in this pattern.
Kein is the usual basic A1 negation for 'not a problem'.

memorization_list.english: not — with verbs, adjectives, adverbs, or specific sentence parts

mastery_goal: You can choose between nicht and kein in common A1 sentences and form simple negative statements.
